actual_derivation.proof: Frozen Revision 2 Definition 1.1 allows constraint multiset IDs and values them uniformly. Theorem 1.6 supplies, for each fixed epsilon>0, constant alphabets and NP-hard val=1 versus val<=epsilon. Appendix B fixes k0=ceil(4/epsilon), takes sub-soundness epsilon/2, augments both alphabets by Z/k0Z, and creates k0 constraints per old ID. The blocks in B.2/B.3 partition the augmented labels into sizes 4 and 1 for each shift. Old perfect labels with equal new coordinates satisfy every constraint. A previously failing label pair passes at most two shifts; when both labels lie in removed parts the equation 2l=KL-KR mod k0 has at most gcd(2,k0)<=2 solutions. Thus final value<=old value+2/k0<=epsilon, including even k0. This source alone gives no biregularity.

For E original constraint IDs remove isolated points; create d_u clones of each endpoint. Each original e=(u,v) generates all d_ud_v clone pairs with its own projection and weight 1/(d_ud_v); each clone has weighted degree 1, total weight E. Independently choosing one clone label for each original vertex maps any clone labeling to an original randomized labeling of equal expected score; copying an original optimum gives the reverse inequality. Weighted values are exactly equal. With S=sum_e d_ud_v<=E^3 and D=ceil(S/(eta E)), the fractional multiplicities D/(d_ud_v) have integer row/column sums D. Floors plus a capacity-one integral bipartite residual flow round each ID/pair to floor or ceil while preserving all D degrees. Per-labeling normalized score error is <=S/(DE)<=eta uniformly, so the optima differ by <=eta without a union bound. Original perfect labels satisfy every retained edge and every original projection remains exact4. There are DE=O(E^3/eta) explicit constraints; eta is fixed before input size. Use source epsilon=zeta/2 and eta=zeta/2.

For fixed L,T set Q=TL+L-1. Layer l consists of a type set A subset[Q] with |A|=l-1, U variables at A and V variables elsewhere; positions may repeat original vertices and carry separate label coordinates. n_l=C(Q,l-1)|U|^(l-1)|V|^(Q-l+1); K_l=k^(l-1)m^(Q-l+1), m=4k. For l<lprime choose h=lprime-l V positions H and one incident source ID e_j per changed position. Replace them by their U endpoints and use the corresponding projections, keeping all other coordinates by identity. Each layer constraint retains H and every source ID; its exact fiber size is r_h=4^h. The negative l-lprime exponents and replacement count actually printed on KS14 physical pp8/20/29 are local reversed signs; the current typed construction uses the correct positive h.

If source degrees on V,U are b,a, each layer-l vertex has outdegree C(Q-l+1,h)b^h and each layer-lprime vertex indegree C(lprime-1,h)a^h, both constant. Uniform source-layer vertex, uniform H and uniform incident IDs generate the uniform layer constraint; its target vertex is uniform by source biregularity. A distinguished replaced coordinate has each source ID with probability 1/(|V|b)=1/|F|. For arbitrary labels on the two layers, fix A,H,j and all other coordinates/IDs. The remaining label at j on the source depends only on its V endpoint, the target label only on its U endpoint; neither endpoint tuple exposes the distinguished ID. Thus they define a legal original source strategy, even with repeated variable names and parallel constraints with different projections. Whole layer-constraint satisfaction implies distinguished-coordinate satisfaction, giving every pair-of-layers value <=source value<=zeta.

If two source tuple labels differ at a U position, that difference survives by identity. Otherwise fix a differing V position j; collision requires j in H, so its probability is <=h/(Q-l+1)<=1/T over incident IDs. For density, start from a uniform all-V tuple and convert a uniformly chosen remaining V position through a uniform incident ID at each step. All layer marginals are uniform; for l,lprime every selected H has h! orders and yields the uniform layer-constraint joint distribution. For s>=ceil(2/rho) sets of layer density>=rho, chain hit count X satisfies EX>=s rho>=2 and E binom(X,2)>=(EX^2-EX)/2>=s^2 rho^2/4. Some layer-pair hit rate is >=rho^2/2, which is stronger than the required rho^2/4. Both properties are by ID counts, never by distinct-neighbor counts.

actual_derivation.step: Heavy blocks and finite analytic constants
actual_derivation.proof: Take rational 0<alpha<min(delta,1/2), L=ceil(32alpha^-2), and fixed rational noise theta in (0,1/2). From independent weighted mass>=alpha, heavy blocks of internal density>=alpha/2 have positive density on at least alpha L/4 layers; using rho=alpha/4 and weak density gives a pair with >=alpha^2/64 heavy constraint IDs. For each of the finitely many r_h=4^h apply the KS14 Section 5 analytic argument with the corrected Gaussian correlation parameter rho0=sqrt(theta)<1 described below. First choose nu_h, then gamma_h,tau_h,s_h and T_h. Set T>=max_h T_h and rational 0<zeta<min_h alpha^2 tau_h^2 gamma_h^2/(2048r_h). Only then choose FMW alphabet bound and eta=zeta/2. All analytic constants are dimension-free and positive, so there is no circular dependence on the eventual long-code dimension.

Each layer variable v gets its full Boolean long-code block {±1}^{K_l}; each codeword has weight 2^-K_l/(L n_l), so each layer has mass 1/L. For each ID projection take all triples in the support of the product D_{theta,r_h} test, with x in the upper block and y,z in the lower block. Color a codeword by its perfect-label coordinate. At the matching coordinate, y,z are either opposite or both equal -x, so no triple is monochromatic. Each fiber has r_h>=4 coordinates and at most one is modified; an unmodified coordinate has y=-z, proving y and z are distinct. x lies in a different layer block, so all three vertices are distinct. Duplicate output three-sets may be merged without changing colorability or independence. Original source constraints may not be deduplicated.

actual_derivation.step: NO decoding and actual ID interface
actual_derivation.proof: An independent set makes the indicator-product expectation zero separately for every projection ID, even if their resulting hyperedges were merged. Lemma 5.14 uses a single projection; Lemma 5.15 bounds nonshattering by s_h^2/T under the incident-ID smoothness distribution. Markov and layer biregularity leave >=alpha^2/128 heavy-good IDs. Influence comparison and Eq33 decode with probability >=tau_h^2 gamma_h^2/(16r_h) on each such ID; labels are sampled from vertex functions independently of which incident ID is tested. Linearity of expectation yields layer-pair value >=alpha^2 tau_h^2 gamma_h^2/(2048r_h)>zeta, contradicting source soundness. A different good coordinate for parallel IDs causes no problem because the vertex labeling distribution is common and the proof sums per ID.

Let Kmax=max_l K_l and B=L(product_l n_l)2^Kmax. Replace each original codeword x in layer l by Bw_x=(product_{j!=l} n_j)2^(Kmax-K_l) clones, a positive integer; total vertex count is B. Replace each original three-point edge by all triples with one clone from each of its three distinct clouds. If a clone independent set occupies all three clouds of an original edge, one occupied clone from each is an edge, contradiction. Its occupied original vertices therefore form an independent set, and its size is at most the sum of full cloud sizes. Conversely every original independent set expands to all its clouds. Consequently alpha(H_unweighted)/B equals the maximum original weighted independent mass exactly. Copy the perfect coloring to every clone cloud. Fixed delta makes L,T,Q,K_l constants, n_l a fixed input-size power, and B and complete edge expansion polynomial. This pays the finite unweighted target, without a simple-source or constant-max-degree assumption.

direct_y_to_z_fourier_bridge.location: Physical pp24-25 / printed pp23-24, Lemma5.18 proof and its use of 5.9(iv).
direct_y_to_z_fourier_bridge.conditional_kernel: The final Y is uniform in every B,J branch, so conditioning on Y does not change P(B=1)=theta or J uniform. Conditional on Y=y, Z=-y with probability1-theta; with probabilitytheta choose J uniform and set Z_J=y_J, Z_i=-y_i for i!=J.
direct_y_to_z_fourier_bridge.walsh_action: For A subset[r], chi_A(z)=(-1)^|A| chi_A(y) on B=0, while B=1 adds a further -1 iff J in A. Therefore E[chi_A(Z)|Y=y]=lambda_A chi_A(y), lambda_A=(-1)^|A|(1-2theta|A|/r).
direct_y_to_z_fourier_bridge.maximal_correlation: For0<theta<1/2 and nonempty A, all 1-2theta|A|/r are positive and decrease with |A|, so max_{A nonempty}|lambda_A|=1-2theta/r=1-eta. The uniform Walsh basis diagonalizes the self-adjoint kernel; this is its exact nonconstant operator norm.
direct_y_to_z_fourier_bridge.tail_bound: Across independent fibers, a Fourier mode supported on b nonempty fibers has eigenvalue magnitude <=(1-eta)^b. An ordinary Fourier character of total Boolean degree>=s occupies at least s/r fibers. Thus the high-degree f1 of Section5.3.2 obeys |E[f_v(Y) f1(Z)]| <=(1-eta)^(s/r)||f_v||_2||f1||_2, exactly the estimate needed in Lemma5.18. There is even a stronger ordinary-degree estimate, but it is unnecessary.
direct_y_to_z_fourier_bridge.existing_s_suffices: The current choice s>= (r/xi)log(1/nu) gives (1-eta)^(s/r)<=exp(-eta s/r)<=nu because eta/xi=2^(r+1)>=1. Hence no new dimension or alphabet dependency enters and the existing s/T selection structure is preserved.
